articles.title: Tech Life - Does the gaming industry have a climate problem? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Video gaming is huge - it's more lucrative than the movies and music combined.
articles.body:
World Service , · 17 Nov 2026 , · 26 mins

Millions of us play on consoles, laptops and phones - it's big business. Grand Theft Auto 6 is the latest blockbuster release. But is gaming having an impact on the environment? Our BBC World Service colleagues at The Climate Question have been looking at gaming and the effect it has on the climate. Jordan Dunbar presents the latest edition, and he joins us on Tech Life to talk about the issues. Also in this episode, we hear from the huge Chinese tech company Tencent about their investment plans. And we find out about the specialised computer chip designed to process AI on your devices. articles.title: Your sneakers could be making plantar fasciitis much worse — try one of these podiatrist-approved pairs instead
articles.summary: Podiatrists recommend the best sneakers for plantar fasciitis that have arch support, shock absorption and rigidity, with expert tips for treating foot pain.
articles.body: One of the first things you should do if you’re diagnosed with plantar fasciitis is closely examine your footwear, says Dr. Priya Parthasarathy, a podiatrist at the Foot & Ankle Specialists of the Mid-Atlantic. Wearing supportive, well-structured shoes is part of treating the condition, which causes pain in the plantar fascia, a ligament that runs along the bottom of the foot to support it — in fact, the wrong shoes can make you even more uncomfortable and extend your recovery timeline. If you’re specifically interested in the best sneakers for plantar fasciitis, there’s a few key features to look for, according to podiatrists I talked to: arch support, a deep heel cup, a firm heel counter, a thick sole, a rigid yet semi-flexible feel, a stable base and removable insoles. Below, I break down how to find a pair of sneakers that make your feet more comfortable rather than aggravate plantar fasciitis. Podiatrists also share their top picks from brands like Hoka, Brooks, New Balance and Skechers, and explain how footwear fits into a larger treatment plan. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best sneakers for plantar fasciitis There isn’t one “best overall” sneaker for plantar fasciitis, says Parthasarathy. Everyone’s feet are different, so while certain features make a sneaker ideal for those with the condition, you also need to consider factors like arch type, foot width and general fit and feel preferences. With that in mind, I curated a list of podiatrist-recommended sneakers for plantar fasciitis to browse through, including options for everyday wear and exercise. Each shoe meets the criteria experts say is important to look for while shopping, and is available in men’s and women’s sizes. For more personalized recommendations, talk to your podiatrist. I noted which sneakers on this list have the American Podiatric Medical Association’s Seal of Acceptance, something shoes earn if they meet specific criteria regarding foot health. Brands voluntarily submit their shoes to the APMA to evaluate — if a pair doesn’t have the seal, it may just mean the APMA hasn’t reviewed them yet, so still consider them if they align with your needs. I also labeled which type of arch support each shoe has: neutral for neutral arches, high for high arches and stability for flat arches. Best for neutral arches I’ve tested almost every pair of Brooks sneakers, and the Glycerins have always been one of my top three favorites for easy runs, walking and daily commuting around New York City. Parthasarathy recommends them for people who have plantar fasciitis and neutral arches. They’re comfortable regardless of how long I wear them for and what I’m doing, and their wide base makes me feel extra stable as I move. Brooks also strategically put the most foam in the heel and forefoot (the area under the ball of your foot) — as you land on your heel, the foam absorbs shock, and as you take off, the foam gives you a boost so you spring off your toes. I’m also a fan of the stretchy heel loop and fabric around the collar of the shoes, which makes it easy to pull on and off my feet. Best for high arches The Hoka Bondi 9 has a pronounced rocker-shaped outsole, which takes stress off the plantar fascia while stretching it, says Pourziaee. It also rolls you forward a bit, causing you to use less energy as you move through strides. The Bondi is Hoka’s plushest, most cushioned everyday road running and walking sneaker, giving it tons of shock absorption, which is especially important if you have high arches, and a soft, bouncy feel. There’s such a thick layer of cushioning that it lifts you off the ground by a few inches, which may make some people feel unstable, says Parthasarathy. She cautions against wearing the Bondis if you have balance issues, and doesn’t recommend them for older adults. Additionally, these sneakers are designed with Hoka’s Active Foot Frame, which some people call a “bucket seat” — your foot sits deep in the midsole (the middle part of the shoe) instead of on top of it, adding stability and preventing the heel from moving around a lot, key for those with plantar fasciitis. Best for flat feet (low arches) If you have plantar fasciitis and flat feet that cause you to overpronate, Pourziaee recommends Brooks’ Adrenaline GTS sneakers. They have the brand’s stability system built-in, hence the “GTS” (a.k.a. Go-To-Support) in the shoe’s name. It’s composed of GuideRails, which are J-shaped strips of stiff material in the midsole that wrap around your heel and toward your arch, essentially acting as bumpers that prevent your ankles from rolling inward too much so you maintain proper alignment. Pourziaee says he typically suggests orthotics for patients with flat feet, but if they don’t want to use them, these sneakers are a good alternative since they’re specifically structured to reduce overpronation. The Adrenaline GTS are a road running and walking shoe, and, like the Glycerins, the soft cushioning is concentrated in the heel and forefoot. Best slip-ins When I talked to Parthasarathy, she was wearing the Skechers Aero Burst sneakers, which she finds comfortable to wear when she’s on her feet seeing patients all day, as well as when she’s walking and running. The shoes are specifically designed to be easy to slip your feet into, preventing you from having to bend down to get them on and off. They have a thick layer of responsive foam, as well as a very firm heel counter and the brand’s HeelPillow, an extra piece of padding that hugs the back of your heel to make feet feel secure and locked in while you move. There’s also a stabilizing H-shaped, carbon-infused plate in the Aero Burst’s midsole. Best for walking “The Hoka Clifton is a nice, neutral shoe that works well for a lot of different foot types,” says Parthasarathy. I’ve worn a pair for about a year, and as someone who prefers a highly cushioned sneaker but doesn’t want to feel like I’m sinking into too-soft foam, they’re exactly what I look for. The foam feels balanced (it lands somewhere between firm and squishy) and it’s lightweight, so I never feel like I’m dragging my feet. And while the rocker-shaped outsole is less pronounced compared to Hoka’s Bondi sneaker, it still rolls me forward enough to help me keep my momentum up. I use the Cliftons, which have Hoka’s Active Foot Frame, as walking and commuting shoes, but Hoka says they’re designed for everyday road runs, too. Best neutral running shoe The New Balance Fresh Foam X 880v15, which comes recommended by Parthasarathy, is a well-cushioned, basic, no frills running sneaker that I also enjoy walking in. It’s designed to keep runners’ feet comfortable, not impact how they move, so they’re best for neutral arches. The sneakers’ foam is on the softer side, but it has some bounce to it, so I never feel like I’m sinking into the midsole. Best stabilizing running shoe Pourziaee recommends the Asics Gel Kayano 32 for runners with plantar fasciitis, and since they’re designed with stabilizing features, they’re especially ideal for those with flat feet, although the brand says they’re great for neutral arches, too. The sneakers have a thick layer of cushioning and a specialized gel material in the heel, giving them maximum shock absorption — that’s something you need to protect your body from miles of repetitive pounding motion. The Kayanos also have a wide base to reduce excess foot movement, which the brand says can cause injury, especially as your legs get tired across long distances. There’s a heel loop to help you slide the sneakers on and off, and reflective details to make your feet more visible in low light, like when you’re jogging around sunrise and sunset. Best for everyday wear The New Balance 990v6 is one of Pourziaee’s top picks for everyday wear, so you can throw them on while you’re running errands, going to work or doing other activities and feel confident that they won’t bother your plantar fasciitis. He says the sneaker’s extra firm heel counter is a standout feature, along with its overall sturdy structure and moderately cushioned midsole. There’s also reflective accents on the shoe, which has suede accents to give it some style. While the women’s version of the 990v6 comes in four widths, which is typical for New Balance sneakers, the men’s version comes in six widths: standard, wide, extra wide, extra extra wide, narrow and extra narrow. How I picked the best sneakers for plantar fasciitis To pick the best sneakers for plantar fasciitis, I asked podiatrists to share their top picks, all of which are ideal for those with the condition because they have the essential features I outlined below. Arch support: Before you shop for sneakers, use our guide (or visit a professional fitter) to determine your arch type: neutral, flat or high. Each one requires different support features, and if you wear the wrong shoe for your arches, you’ll likely feel a burning, achy sensation on the bottom of your feet, which can exacerbate plantar fasciitis. One of the easiest ways to tell if a shoe has arch support in general is to try to bend it in half — if it folds easily, it has little to no arch support, says Parthasarathy.Deep heel cup: Plantar fasciitis pain usually starts in and is concentrated around the heel, so extra heel support is a must when it comes to sneakers. Look for a deep heel cup, which is a slightly inset U-shaped part of a shoe’s insole that holds the heel bone (the calcaneus) in place to support it and prevent it from moving around too much, says Pourziaee. This part of the insole also absorbs shock to protect the heel bone.Firm heel counter: The heel counter is an area in the back of the shoe that cups the heel bone from a different angle compared to the heel cup, offering additional support. It similarly provides stability and prevents excess movement. Some heel counters are soft and flimsy, which doesn’t do much for you. Instead, you want a firm heel counter: You can tell a sneaker has a firm heel counter if you squeeze the back of the shoe and it doesn’t collapse completely, says Parthasarathy.Well-cushioned midsole: Cushioning in a sneaker’s midsole absorbs shock every time you take a step, softening your landings and reducing how much impact your feet feel, especially around the inflamed plantar fascia ligament and painful heel area, says Pourziaee. You don’t need to buy sneakers with a multi-inch layer of foam if you don’t like the feel of them, but they should have a noticeable layer of padding to avoid further straining the plantar fascia.Structure balanced with flexibility: Rigid shoes that have a clear structure to them help your feet go through all phases of a gait cycle (flat foot, heel off, toe off) and prevent the plantar fascia from getting strained, says Pourziaee. But some flexibility is still important. “You want to make sure that the shoe bends at the ball of the foot, but you can’t squish or fold it in other places,” he says. You also shouldn’t be able to twist the shoe so much that you’re essentially wringing it out like a wet cloth while holding both ends.Removable insole: Being able to remove the insole a sneaker comes with and swap it for a better over-the-counter option, or an orthotic a podiatrist makes for you, lets you customize the shoe to better support your feet. Before you buy a pair of sneakers, podiatrists also recommend thinking about what activities you want to do while wearing them, like running, walking and training. It’s essential to wear the right shoe for the right activity — if you don’t, your feet won’t be properly supported, which can aggravate conditions like plantar fasciitis. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Priya Parthasarathy is a podiatrist at the Foot & Ankle Specialists of the Mid-Atlantic.Dr. Bobby Pourziaee is a podiatrist at Rodeo Drive Podiatry based in Beverly Hills, California. I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has covered fitness apparel and footwear for over five years, writing about topics like women’s walking shoes, women’s running shoes, training shoes, carbon-plated running shoes and running shoes with arch support. For this story, I interviewed two experts about sneakers for plantar fasciitis and rounded up their favorite options. I also test dozens of pairs of sneakers a year across brands to stay updated on the newest models. articles.title: Rochdale's landmark Seven Sisters tower blocks to be demolished
articles.summary: The landlord says refurbishment would have cost at least £269m, while replacing them was "affordable".
articles.body:
A town's landmark tower blocks, which have dominated its skyline since the 1960s, are set to be demolished after years of uncertainty over their future.

Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes, social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) said.

Residents began moving out of the flats in October 2025 following concerns about their long-term safety but a local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished.

But RBH said replacing the buildings was the "only realistic and affordable way" to provide suitable homes for residents.

Refurbishment would have cost at least £269m and would have taken 12 years, RBH said.

Some 78 households have yet to accept an offer of another home.

Previous building surveys have identified structural and electrical issues with the tower blocks, and problems with water pumps and roof damage.

RBH said it expected all remaining residents would be supported to move out by August 2027. One of the blocks, Mitchell Hey, has already closed.

RBH Chief Executive Amanda Newton said: "College Bank has been home to generations of Rochdalians, and we recognise the important place the blocks hold in many people's memories."

She said replacing the buildings was the "only realistic and affordable way" to provide homes.

Plans to demolish the towers were first revealed in 2017, prompting opposition from residents, and demolition was ruled out in 2023.

RBH subsequently said all options were back on the table.

The social landlord said the proposed 601 new homes could accommodate more people, despite being fewer in number, with at least 249 additional bedspaces.

RBH said it hoped some former residents could return to College Bank once the new homes were built, although this had yet to be agreed.

The redevelopment will require planning permission, and RBH did not give a demolition date in its announcement.

articles.title: Prefeitura de Feira de Santana publica decretos de desapropriação | G1
articles.standfirst: Áreas ficam no bairro Sim e incluem partes de imóveis comerciais, edificações e terrenos. Medidas foram publicadas no Diário Oficial desta terça-feira (17).
articles.summary: Áreas ficam no bairro Sim e incluem partes de imóveis comerciais, edificações e terrenos. Medidas foram publicadas no Diário Oficial desta terça-feira (17).
articles.body:
Avenida Artêmia Pires, em Feira de Santana — Foto: Fotos ilustrativas: ACM

A Prefeitura de Feira de Santana , segunda maior cidade da Bahia, publicou mais 15 decretos de desapropriação de áreas para a duplicação da Avenida Artêmia Pires Freitas, no bairro Sim.

As medidas constam na edição do Diário Oficial do Município desta terça-feira (17) e declaram os espaços de utilidade pública, em regime de urgência.

Entre os imóveis mencionados nos documentos estão estabelecimentos comerciais, como barbearias, restaurantes e uma drogaria. As áreas atingidas variam de 15,37 m² a 615,06 m² e incluem partes de construções, muros e coberturas.

Os decretos foram assinados pelo prefeito José Ronaldo de Carvalho e entraram em vigor com a publicação. Os documentos não informam os valores das indenizações nem estabelecem prazos para a desocupação dos espaços.

Na última sexta-feira (13), mais 21 terrenos foram declarados de utilidade pública para permitir a ampliação da Avenida Artêmia Pires Freitas. Na quinta-feira (12), outros 19 imóveis já haviam sido incluídos no processo.

A obra prevê a duplicação dos 7 km da Artêmia Pires, no trecho que vai do Anel de Contorno até o Condomínio Dahma, incluindo execução de drenagem de águas pluviais, redes de esgotamento sanitário, implantação de passeios, moderna iluminação pública e nova sinalização.

Além da duplicação total, o projeto inclui transformar em mão única o trecho que começa no Anel de Contorno e segue pela área da Faculdade Unex. Veja as principais mudanças previstas no trânsito com a duplicação:

Mão única entre a Unex no sentido Anel de Contorno;

Construção de um viaduto na saída da Artêmia Pires em direção ao Centro da cidade;

Implantação de três pistas entre a Unex e a Avenida Fernando Pinto de Queiroz;

Após a Avenida Fernando Pinto de Queiroz, a via passará a contar com quatro pistas;

Obras de infraestrutura e pavimentação para urbanizar ruas e avenidas que ligarão a Artêmia Pires às avenidas Sérgio Carneiro, Sílvio Matos e Eduardo Fróes da Motta (Anel de Contorno).

A intervenção também prevê urbanização, nova sinalização viária e sistema de drenagem em toda a via.

De acordo com estimativas da prefeitura, a Avenida Artêmia Pires chega a receber quase 3 mil veículos por hora nos horários de pico. A expectativa é de que a duplicação e as mudanças planejadas ampliem a capacidade de tráfego e reduzam o tempo de deslocamento dos moradores da região.

articles.title: Caças dos EUA atacam ilha do Irã em primeira ofensiva após midterms | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação militar atingiu a ilha de Qeshm, no sul do país, segundo fontes do governo norte-americano. A ofensiva, caso confirmada, marca retomada dos EUA contra o Irã desde as eleições de meio de mandato norte-americanas.
articles.summary: Ação militar atingiu ilha de Qeshm, no sul do país, segundo uma fonte do governo norte-americano disse à agência de notícias Reuters.
articles.body:
Cartaz em Teerã faz montagem do Estreito de Ormuz sobre o rosto de Donald Trump, em 4 de maio de 2026. — Foto: Wana via Reuters

Os Estados Unidos atacaram nesta terça-feira (17) uma base iraniana na ilha de Qeshm, no sul do Irã , segundo fontes do governo norte-americano confirmaram às agências de notícias Reuters e AFP.

👉 Se confirmado, o ataque marca a retomada de ataques dos EUA ao Irã após uma pausa nas operações militares durante as eleições de meio de mandato norte-americanas, no início de novembro, em que o partido de Donald Trump foi derrotado — avaliações apontaram a guerra contra o Irã como um dos principais fatores da derrota.

Segundo as fontes ouvidas pela Reuters e pela AFP, caças dos EUA alvejaram uma base de lançamento de mísseis da ilha de Qeshm, em uma represália a ações do Irã contra pessoal e ativos norte-americanos no Golfo Pérsico — nesta semana, Teerã atacou bases dos EUA no Bahrein .

Caças americanos "utilizaram munições de precisão para atacar, em legítima defesa, uma base de lançamento de mísseis do Corpo da Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica [IRGC, na sigla em inglês] na ilha de Qeshm", declarou à AFP o representante americano, sob condição de anonimato.

O governo dos EUA ainda não havia confirmado de forma oficial o ataque. Mais cedo, agências de notícias iranianas afirmaram que moradores da ilha relataram explosões. A agência estatal iraniana Fars disse ainda que drones do tipo LUCAS atingiram o local.

A ilha de Qeshm fica no Estreito de Ormuz, uma das principais rotas marítimas para o transporte mundial de petróleo. A região tem sido um dos focos de tensão entre Washington e Teerã desde o início da guerra, em 28 de fevereiro.

O presidente Donald Trump havia sinalizado que os Estados Unidos suspenderiam os ataques antes das eleições de meio de mandato, realizadas em 3 de novembro. O republicano também indicou que não pretendia retomar os bombardeios após a votação, em meio às negociações com o governo iraniano.

articles.title: Chuvas em SE inundam estação e suspendem produção de água tratada | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidade teve equipamentos submersos durante a madrugada; Deso informou que ainda analisa os impactos provocados pela cheia e não divulgou o número de pessoas afetadas.
articles.summary: Devido às fortes chuvas em Poço Redondo, a inundação da ETA Curralinho deixou bombas submersas e a Deso avalia danos para retomar a produção de água na região.
articles.body:
Chuvas inundam estação de tratamento e suspendem produção de água em Poço Redondo — Foto: Deso/Divulgação

As fortes chuvas registradas no estado provocaram a inundação da casa de bombas da Estação de Tratamento de Água (ETA) Curralinho, localizada no município de Poço Redondo , e interromperam a produção de água tratada na unidade nesta terça-feira (17).

De acordo com a Companhia de Saneamento de Sergipe (Deso), a ocorrência foi registrada por volta das 3h30, quando a água invadiu as instalações e deixou os conjuntos de bombeamento da estação submersos.

Segundo a companhia, equipes técnicas estão avaliando os danos causados pela inundação e estudando medidas necessárias para restabelecer a operação no menor prazo possível.

A Deso não informou quantas pessoas foram afetadas pela interrupção da produção de água tratada.

articles.title: Lixo, queima de fios e furtos preocupam moradores da Vila Nhanhá | G1
articles.standfirst: Acúmulo de resíduos às margens do córrego Anhanduí, fumaça da queima de cobre e crimes frequentes afetam a rotina de quem vive e trabalha na região. Moradores cobram providências das autoridades.
articles.summary: Acúmulo de resíduos às margens do córrego Anhanduí, fumaça da queima de cobre e crimes frequentes afetam a rotina de quem vive e trabalha na região.
articles.body:
A região da Vila Nhanhá, em Campo Grande , preocupa moradores e comerciantes. Furtos, roubos, ameaças e a presença frequente de usuários de drogas estão entre as principais reclamações de quem vive e trabalha no local, que também abrange bairros como Marcos Roberto e Jóquei Clube.

Além dos problemas relacionados à segurança, moradores e comerciantes denunciam o descarte irregular de lixo às margens do córrego Anhanduí. Uma grande quantidade de resíduos se acumula no local, às margens da avenida Ernesto Geisel, uma das principais vias da capital.

Outro problema é a queima de fios de cobre, que, segundo os moradores, são furtados de casas, comércios e da própria rede de energia. A fumaça das fogueiras feitas às margens do córrego também afeta quem vive e trabalha na região.

O empresário Valdo Silva, proprietário de uma empresa de inspeção veicular, afirma que perdeu clientes por causa da situação. Segundo ele, o medo de furtos faz com que algumas pessoas evitem levar os veículos ao estabelecimento.

"Não tem como reclamar, eles são agressivos. Quanto a clientela, eles ficam com medo de trazer o carro, deixar na frente do comércio, e vir alguém mexer ou furtar um pneu. A gente entende o medo do cliente, porque realmente a gente está a mercê da situação", conta.

A aposentada Maria Marlene Silveira de Lima, que faz tratamento contra o câncer, relata dificuldades para respirar por causa da fumaça.

"Prejudica bastante, porque a gente tem que estar mesmo no frio com o ventilador ligado, e aquele ar pesado. A gente se sente sufocados dentro de casa", relata.

O dono de uma oficina mecânica, Marcos Antônio Soares, também reclama dos efeitos da fumaça no ambiente de trabalho. "A fumaça entra toda aqui dentro da oficina, a gente não consegue trabalhar direito lá dentro, muita fumaça", relata.

Furtos frequentes aumentam sensação de insegurança

Além do lixo e da fumaça, moradores da Vila Nhanhá, do Marcos Roberto e de outros bairros próximos relatam medo de furtos a qualquer hora do dia. Segundo eles, os criminosos levam fios de cobre, padrões de energia, hidrômetros e objetos deixados dentro de veículos.

O marceneiro Hildo Francisco Boldori diz que já teve o estabelecimento furtado cerca de 15 vezes. Para evitar novos prejuízos, ele precisa levar as ferramentas para casa ao fim do expediente.

"A gente não tem sossego, quando eu saio da marcenaria e vou pra minha casa, tenho que levar todas as minhas ferramentas manuais. As poucas vezes que deixei me roubaram furadeira, parafusadeira, compressor de ar grande, fiação, roubaram tudo, não temos mais fiação de metal, é tudo aluminio porque se não eles roubam tudo", conta.

Os moradores cobram providências das autoridades para combater os furtos e o consumo de drogas na região. Eles relatam que parte dos crimes é praticada para conseguir dinheiro para sustentar o vício.

Em nota, a Polícia Militar informou que realiza patrulhamento preventivo diário na região, com equipes do 1º Batalhão e unidades especializadas. A corporação também afirmou que encaminhará as reclamações dos moradores à unidade responsável para avaliar a situação e, se necessário, reforçar as ações de segurança.

A PM orienta a população a registrar boletins de ocorrência e comunicar situações suspeitas. Denúncias anônimas podem ser feitas pelo telefone 181. Em casos de emergência, o contato é o 190.

A Secretaria Municipal de Assistência Social (SAS) informou que o Serviço Especializado em Abordagem Social funciona 24 horas por dia, todos os dias da semana, nas sete regiões de Campo Grande.

Segundo a pasta, as equipes fazem buscas ativas, atendem denúncias e identificam locais com maior concentração de pessoas em situação de rua. As abordagens são intensificadas na região central e em pontos como viadutos, pontes, praças e na avenida Ernesto Geisel.

A secretaria ressaltou, porém, que nem todas as pessoas que ficam nos semáforos da avenida estão em situação de rua. Durante as abordagens, as equipes identificaram pessoas que moram no próprio bairro e utilizam os semáforos para complementar a renda.

Sobre os usuários de substâncias psicoativas, a SAS afirmou que muitos recusam o encaminhamento para comunidades terapêuticas por dificuldades em iniciar o tratamento. A pasta explicou que o acolhimento é voluntário e que a recusa é um direito garantido pela Constituição Federal. Quando há aceitação, a pessoa pode ser encaminhada para uma das duas unidades de acolhimento do município ou para uma comunidade terapêutica.

Denúncias e solicitações de abordagem podem ser feitas diretamente à SAS pelos telefones 99660-6539, 99660-1469 e 156.

articles.title: ENAC: mais de 7,6 mil candidatos farão exame nacional obrigatório para concursos de cartórios | G1
articles.standfirst: Criado pelo CNJ, ENAC funciona como etapa prévia aos concursos estaduais e concede habilitação válida por seis anos. Mais de 4,5 mil candidatos já foram habilitados desde 2025.
articles.summary: Criado pelo CNJ, ENAC funciona como etapa prévia aos concursos estaduais e concede habilitação válida por seis anos. Mais de 4,5 mil candidatos já foram habilitados desde 2025.
articles.body:
Sede do Conselho Nacional de Justiça. — Foto: Rômulo Serpa/Agência CNJ

Mais de 7,6 mil candidatos em todo o país vão participar, no próximo domingo (22), da quarta edição do Exame Nacional dos Cartórios (ENAC), prova que se tornou uma etapa obrigatória para quem deseja participar de concursos públicos para assumir a titularidade de cartórios.

Segundo a Corregedoria Nacional de Justiça, responsável pela organização da avaliação, foram homologadas 7.640 inscrições nesta edição.

Criado pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ), o exame funciona como uma espécie de filtro nacional.

🔎 Antes da criação do exame, o candidato podia se inscrever diretamente nos concursos organizados pelos tribunais de Justiça dos estados. Agora, é preciso primeiro obter a habilitação no ENAC para depois participar dessas seleções.

A prova não serve para classificar os participantes por nota nem substitui as etapas dos concursos. O objetivo é verificar se os candidatos têm o conhecimento jurídico mínimo necessário para disputar as seleções para cartórios em todo o país.

🎓 Para participar das seleções, os interessados precisam ter diploma de bacharel em Direito reconhecido pelo Ministério da Educação (MEC) ou comprovar pelo menos 10 anos de experiência em serviços notariais ou de registro.

A iniciativa foi aprovada pelo CNJ em 2024 e passou por ajustes até ser incorporada às regras nacionais dos concursos de cartórios, estabelecidas pela Resolução CNJ nº 696/2026.

Quem são os candidatos e como será a prova

Dos 7.640 candidatos com inscrição homologada, 3.520 são mulheres e 4.120 são homens . Entre os inscritos, também há 933 pessoas negras, 1.015 pessoas com deficiência e 78 indígenas.

O exame será aplicado simultaneamente nas capitais estaduais e no Distrito Federal. Os candidatos terão cinco horas para responder a 100 questões de múltipla escolha, das 14h às 19h (horário de Brasília).

Para ser considerado habilitado, o participante deverá acertar pelo menos 60% das questões. No caso dos candidatos que concorrem pelas políticas de ações afirmativas, o percentual mínimo exigido é de 50%.

A maior parte das questões, 60 ao todo, será dedicada aos conteúdos diretamente ligados às atividades dos cartórios. As outras 40 abordarão diferentes áreas do Direito, como Direito Constitucional, Civil, Administrativo, Tributário, Empresarial, Penal e Trabalhista.

Segundo o CNJ, a avaliação foi elaborada para avaliar não apenas a memorização de conteúdos, mas também a capacidade dos candidatos de aplicar conhecimentos jurídicos em situações práticas. Quem for aprovado receberá uma habilitação com validade de seis anos .

Durante esse período, o candidato poderá usar a habilitação para se inscrever em concursos públicos para assumir a titularidade de cartórios, desde que cumpra as regras específicas de cada edital.

A regulamentação prevê ainda que o exame seja realizado pelo menos duas vezes por ano. A proposta é estabelecer um padrão nacional de qualificação para quem deseja assumir a titularidade de cartórios em qualquer estado do país.

Desde a primeira edição do ENAC, realizada em 2025, 4.557 candidatos obtiveram a habilitação necessária para disputar concursos de cartórios. Desse total, 2.801 foram aprovados na primeira edição, 916 na segunda e 840 na terceira.

Os dados consolidados do CNJ mostram ainda que, entre os habilitados até agora, há 497 candidatos negros, 582 pessoas com deficiência, sete indígenas e quatro quilombolas.

Para a Corregedoria Nacional de Justiça, o exame busca padronizar a qualificação dos futuros titulares de cartórios em todo o país, estabelecendo um nível mínimo de conhecimento antes mesmo da abertura dos concursos estaduais.

24 de novembro de 2026: divulgação prevista do gabarito

articles.title: Vendedora de brigadeiros é encontrada em abrigo de Cubatão   | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipe do abrigo reconheceu Bruna Martins, de 33 anos, a partir de notícias sobre o desaparecimento e localizou o perfil da prima dela no Instagram.
articles.summary: Equipe do abrigo reconheceu Bruna Martins, de 33 anos, a partir de notícias sobre o desaparecimento e localizou o perfil da prima dela no Instagram.
articles.body:
Vendedora de brigadeiros é encontrada em abrigo de Cubatão após seis dias desaparecida — Foto: Divulgação

A vendedora de brigadeiros Bruna Martins, de 33 anos, foi encontrada nesta terça-feira (17) em um abrigo no bairro Vila Paulista, em Cubatão (SP), após seis dias desaparecida. Segundo a família, ela estava bem quando foi buscada na unidade.

A família informou que Bruna saiu de casa na quarta-feira (11), no bairro Rádio Clube, em Santos. Segundo os familiares, ela tem deficiência intelectual leve e saiu sem o celular e os documentos.

Ao g1 , Vitória Thom, prima de Bruna, contou que a vendedora seguiu a pé em direção a Cubatão e pediu ajuda ao chegar à cidade. Como estava sem documentos, foi orientada a procurar o abrigo.

Na unidade, a equipe encontrou notícias sobre o desaparecimento e localizou o perfil de Vitória no Instagram. "Me ligaram, falaram que ela estava lá e estava bem", disse Vitória. Segundo a prima, a equipe acionou a polícia, e a mãe de Bruna foi até o abrigo buscá-la.

articles.title: Israel: aliado de rival de Netanyahu é eleito presidente do Parlamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Cargo é estratégico para a oposição, que deseja desmantelar o legado legislativo de Benjamin Netanyahu.
articles.summary: Cargo é estratégico para a oposição, que deseja desmantelar o legado legislativo de Benjamin Netanyahu.
articles.body:
Matan Kahana em foto de junho de 2021 — Foto: EMMANUEL DUNAND/AFP

Os parlamentares israelenses votaram nesta terça-feira (17) para eleger Matan Kahana, aliado de Gadi Eisenkot, como presidente do órgão legislativo, uma primeira vitória política para a oposição ao primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu.

Kahana, membro do partido Yashar, foi eleito com 66 dos 120 votos do parlamento, uma vitória que permite que Eisenkot e seu bloco assumam um cargo estratégico, que pode definir o calendário parlamentar e acelerar ou atrasar debates e votações de leis.

Essa é uma ferramenta essencial para a oposição, que deseja desmantelar o mais rapidamente possível o legado legislativo de Netanyahu.

Benjamin Netanyahu e Gadi Eisenkot — Foto: Yonatan Sindel/Pool via REUTERS e REUTERS/Shir Torem

No fim de outubro, a coalizão governista de Netanyahu perdeu maioria no Parlamento israelense e obteve apenas cinco cadeiras a mais que a coalizão de oposição liderada por Gadi Eisenkot. Desde então, os dois blocos travam uma corrida em busca de alianças formar novo governo.

A coalizão de Netanyahu obteve 53 cadeiras . Ela é formada pelos partidos Likud, Shas, UTJ, RZP, Otzma Yehudit. Antes da eleição, a coalizão do premiê detinha a maioria no Knesset, com 63 assentos.

Já a coalizão de oposição, liderada por Eisenkot, obteve 48 cadeiras. Ela é formada pelos partidos Yashar, B'Yachad, Democratas e Yisrael Beiteinu.

👉 Como o Parlamento tem um total de 120 cadeiras, é necessário que uma coalizão detenha ao menos 61 assentos para formar um novo governo.

Eisenkot foi escolhido para tentar formar novo governo

Há cerca de dez dias, o presidente de Israel, Isaac Herzog, oficializou a escolha para que Gadi Eisenkot tente formar um novo governo.

A escolha foi feita porque a coalizão de Eisenkot é a que tem mais chances de garantir uma maioria no Parlamento. O candidato tem até o início de dezembro para tentar formar um governo. Se necessário, Herzog poderá conceder a ele uma prorrogação de até 14 dias.

➡️ Israel adota o sistema de governo parlamentarista, no qual o partido ou coalizão que obtiverem votos suficientes para formar maioria no Parlamento indica quem será o primeiro-ministro. No caso de nenhum grupo alcançar a maioria, como foi no pleito israelense, o presidente do país, que atua como chefe de Estado, pode escolher quem ele acha ter mais chances de formar governo.

articles.title: Adoção de cartinhas de Natal: Escola em Macapá abre campanha | G1
articles.standfirst: Campanha da Escola Municipal Maestro Miguel, no bairro Perpétuo Socorro, recebe presentes até 15 de dezembro. Entrega às crianças será feita por um Papai Noel no encerramento das aulas.
articles.summary: A campanha de adoção de cartinhas de Natal da Escola Maestro Miguel em Macapá busca padrinhos para presentear 1.200 crianças até o dia 15 de dezembro.
articles.body:
Escola pública de Macapá abre adoção de 1.200 cartinhas de Natal; veja como participar — Foto: Jeferson Gonçalves/Rede Amazônica

🎄- A Escola Municipal Maestro Miguel, localizada no bairro Perpétuo Socorro, em Macapá , abriu para adoção cerca de 1.200 cartinhas de Natal escritas por alunos do 1º ao 5º ano do ensino fundamental. A campanha busca padrinhos na comunidade e entre empresas locais para realizar os pedidos das crianças neste fim de ano .

Para participar, basta ir até a escola e escolher uma ou mais cartinhas nas duas árvores de Natal montadas na instituição — uma para o turno da manhã e outra para o da tarde.

Os presentes devem ser entregues no local até o dia 15 de dezembro . A entrega oficial aos estudantes será feita por um Papai Noel no dia 18 de dezembro, data do encerramento das aulas.

Entre os desejos escritos à mão e ilustrados com desenhos coloridos, aparecem desde materiais escolares até personagens de desenhos animados. O estudante Samuel Brito, de 10 anos, aluno do 5º ano, participa da ação desde o 2º ano e desta vez pediu um kit de desenho.

"Eu vejo na internet e eu desenho várias coisas. Gosto de tudo. Estou bastante ansioso para ganhar o kit", contou Samuel.

Estudante Samuel Brito, de 10 anos. — Foto: Jeferson Gonçalves/Rede Amazônica

Colega de série, Isabela Rodrigues, também de 10 anos, escolheu um boneco do personagem Satoru Gojo, do anime Jujutsu Kaisen. Ela participa da campanha há cinco anos e destaca a empolgação da turma.

"É muito legal. A gente sempre faz esse negócio todo ano. Os colegas acham legal também, na maioria das vezes eles pedem material escolar", disse a aluna.

Estudante Isabela Rodrigues, de 10 anos. — Foto: Jeferson Gonçalves/Rede Amazônica

O projeto Natal Solidário existe há mais de 12 anos. Segundo a coordenadora pedagógica Aline Natividade dos Santos, a iniciativa nasceu da diretora Andrea Penanti, com apoio da coordenação e do professor Benedito, após perceberem as dificuldades financeiras de algumas famílias da região.

"Quem quiser, toda a comunidade, as empresas, parcerias, quiser vir à nossa escola, estamos de portas abertas para recebê-los. Devido ao quantitativo de alunos que nós temos, mais de mil alunos, a gente precisa dessa sensibilização, dessa solidariedade", explicou a coordenadora.

Coordenadora pedagógica Aline Natividade dos Santos. — Foto: Jeferson Gonçalves/Rede Amazônica

Caso alguma cartinha não seja adotada até o prazo final, a própria equipe escolar providencia um presente alternativo para garantir que nenhum estudante fique sem lembrança na festa de encerramento.

Escola pública de Macapá abre adoção de 1.200 cartinhas de Natal; veja como participar. — Foto: Jeferson Gonçalves/Rede Amazônica

A transparência da campanha atrai padrinhos recorrentes, como o professor Eli Ribeiro de Oliveira, que já participava da ação junto com a esposa e decidiu adotar novamente neste ano.

"Esse é um projeto que já vem há muitos anos e é muito transparente. Devido a algumas crianças não terem condições realmente de ter presente, acabam fazendo essa cartinha e esperando que alguém vá presenteá-las", afirmou o padrinho.

Professor Eli Ribeiro de Oliveira. — Foto: Jeferson Gonçalves/Rede Amazônica

articles.title: Starbucks' Red Cup Day is here. What to buy to get a reusable holiday cup today.
articles.summary: The limited-edition red cup is back for one day only. Here's how to get yours.
articles.body:
Starbucks' Red Cup Day has arrived. Today, Nov. 17, customers who buy a holiday or fall drink at participating U.S. stores can get a limited-edition red reusable cup while supplies last.

The giveaway, which applies to iced, blended and hot drinks from the menu, will be available with orders placed in-store, through the Starbucks app, and via DoorDash, Grubhub, or Uber Eats.

This year's design, featuring an illustrated coffee tree branch and coffee cherries, will also give customers the chance to save and earn extra points. Customers who bring in a clean, reusable cup will get a 10-cent discount and double stars if they're a Starbucks Rewards customer.

Today, the Winter Wonderland line also lands: a collection of drinkware in an icy blue-and-white color scheme. There's a quilted cold cup, iridescent water bottles and a snowglobe-topped mug, among other items.

The first of Starbucks' 2026 seasonal offerings dropped Nov. 5, with the return of festive classics as well as the Tiramisu Velvet lineup debut, an Apple Pomegranate Refresher, and new sandwiches and treats.

Stores selling the Surprise Bearista cups, which launched Nov. 10, reported queues around the block to get the cups, echoing last year's frenzy . This year's $39.95 Surprise Box Edition went on sale at select coffeehouses with a limit of two per customer.

A new Bearista Cake Pop and Bearista-themed merchandise have been on sale since Nov. 5, and the original Bearista Glass Cold Cup is due back Dec. 1.

On Nov. 5, four seasonal favorites returned: the Peppermint Mocha, Caramel Brulée Latte, Sugar Cookie Latte and Gingerbread Chai.

The same date saw the launch of the new Apple Pomegranate Refresher, which Starbucks bills as featuring "crisp apple flavors and popping pomegranate-flavored pearls." There will be a creamier alternative available: a Snowy Apple variation, made with coconut milk.

The new Tiramisu Velvet duo arrived on the same day. A twist on the traditional Italian dessert, the Tiramisu Velvet Latte will be available hot or iced, and the Tiramisu Velvet Cold Brew will finish off the collection. Both drinks are, according to Starbucks, topped with a velvet mascarpone cold foam and cocoa and coffee dusting.

The Bearista cup is back, as well as other merchandise

The Bearista Glass Cold Cup returns on Dec. 1, but only to select coffeehouses and while supplies last. The bear-shaped design once again features a green beanie-shaped lid and striped straw.

Ahead of the launch, a new Surprise Box Edition arrived on Nov. 10, featuring a range of five festive character cups made from hand-blown glass. Customers only knew which festive character their box contained after they'd made their purchase. Long queues to get hold of the limited-edition items were reported on the day .

The bears include Aspen, the ski bear; Reiny, the reindeer bear; Bunny, the snow bear; Joy, the ice skating bear; and Goldie, the Golden bear and rarest of the collection.

The holiday tree design cold glass cup was also available to purchase from Nov. 5.

On the same date, drinkware featuring the Bearista motif hit the shelves, along with a miniature plus bear on a keychain and other matching accessories.

There's a Bearista Cake Pop this year too

For the full bear moment, you can pair your Bearista cup with a new Bearista Cake Pop this holiday season. The new cake pop, released earlier this month, is on sale for a limited time. So it's another holiday menu item to get while you can.

Other food items include two sandwiches: the new Braised Short Rib Grilled Cheese and the Turkey & Stuffing Sandwich, which Starbucks says features a new recipe. A sweet treat trio — the Cranberry Bliss Bar, Snowman Cookie and Sugar Plum Cheese Danish — will all be returning.

articles.title: Six in court accused of high-value Pokemon card theft
articles.summary: Six men have been charged in connection with the theft of high-value Pokemon cards from a warehouse.
articles.body:
Six men charged over the theft of high-value Pokemon cards from a warehouse in Nottinghamshire have appeared in court.

Nottinghamshire Police said a group allegedly drilled through the wall of a business premises in Aurillac Way, Retford, before stealing 26 boxes of cards in December.

Liam Duce and Liam Parker, both of HMP Lancaster Farms; Daniel Milligan, 27, of Wharfe Street in Otley; Brandon Coates, of Broom Terrace, Leeds; Matthew Middleton, of Pawson Street, Leeds; and Mohammed Hussan, of Whiteacre Road, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire, were charged with conspiracy to commit burglary between 25 and 28 December.

They appeared at Mansfield Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

Duce, 25, and Parker, 29, appeared in court via video-link from HMP Lancaster Farms, and were remanded in custody.

Coates, 20, Middleton, 44, and Hussan, 32, attended court in person. They were granted bail with conditions, including not to contact their co-defendants and not to go to Obsidia Ltd, a trading card business in Retford.

Milligan, who appeared in court virtually, was also granted conditional bail.

All six defendants were told to appear at Nottingham Crown Court on 15 December for a plea hearing.

articles.title: Iran rejects CNN report of 'dirty bomb' plot in Washington, calls claims 'fabricated'
articles.summary: Iran has firmly rejected CNN's report about a supposed dirty bomb plot in Washington, calling the allegations fabricated and part of a media campaign by the US and Israel for military justification. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei criticized the reports and emphasized Iran's readiness to respond to any aggression.
articles.body: Iran has rejected allegations that it was considering a radioactive dirty bomb attack in Washington, describing a CNN report on the suspected plot as fabricated and accusing the United States and Israel of using media reports to build a case for further military action against Tehran.Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei dismissed the claims in a post on X on Tuesday, also rejecting a separate report by The New York Times that suggested some Iranian dams could be linked to underground missile facilities.“Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations,” Baghaei wrote, referring to the reports by CNN and The New York Times.CNN had reported, citing seven US officials familiar with intelligence assessments, that Iran was exploring possible plans to target senior members of the Trump administration using a radioactive dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, DC.The report said US intelligence had identified specific locations and potential targets. However, officials remained divided over whether Tehran had the capability or intention to carry out an attack. Sources described the activity as an effort to develop possible options rather than evidence of an imminent operation.The White House said it was monitoring potential risks but maintained that there was no credible immediate threat to the United States.Baghaei also challenged the allegations concerning Iranian dams, arguing that the proximity of civilian infrastructure to military facilities did not make those sites legitimate military targets.“Portraying the geographical proximity of civilian infrastructure to military facilities as grounds for designating it a legitimate military target is neither a credible argument nor a substantiated claim,” he said.He described the claims as an attempt to justify attacks on Iran's essential infrastructure and cited recent strikes on water facilities across the country. According to Baghaei, reservoirs in Khomeyn, Haftkel and Bamani were targeted, along with desalination facilities on Qeshm Island, in Nikshahr and Tis, and in the village of Banji in Jask. He alleged that the attacks disrupted or cut off water supplies to civilian communities.The Foreign Ministry spokesman also referred to Article 56 of Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions, which provides special protection to dams and other installations containing dangerous forces under international humanitarian law.Baghaei accused those behind the allegations of attempting to create justification for further action against Iran, warning that the country would respond to any aggression.“Iran knows well how to respond to any act of aggression and ensure that it is met with an unforgettable response,” he wrote.He urged the international community not to remain silent over what he described as attempts to normalise violations of international law, arguing that the consequences could extend beyond the Middle East.You use AI every day. articles.title: After UN peacekeeping mission ends, Morocco says Western Sahara dispute enters new phase
articles.summary: Western Sahara talks enter a new phase as a senior Sahrawi official says Morocco will implement its autonomy proposal even if the Polisario Front refuses to agree.
articles.body: Six years after President Donald Trump recognized Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara, a senior regional official says the decades-old territorial dispute has entered a new phase, with negotiations now focused on how Morocco's autonomy proposal would be implemented following the end of the United Nations peacekeeping mission. Sidi Hamdi Ould Errachid, president of the Laâyoune–Sakia El Hamra Regional Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive Zoom interview that Morocco remains open to negotiations with other parties, but suggested that opposition to the plan would not necessarily prevent it from moving forward. "The Moroccan side remains open to international engagement, and we are prepared to negotiate how the autonomy proposal will be implemented," he said through an interpreter. US COUNTERS CHINA AS BEIJING’S ‘SHOCK WAVE’ HITS AFRICAN ECONOMIES Asked what remains to be negotiated with the Polisario Front, which seeks independence for Western Sahara, Ould Errachid indicated that Morocco intends to pursue its autonomy initiative regardless of whether all parties reach an agreement. "If the other parties do not agree, we will continue implementing the autonomy proposal on the ground," he said through the interpreter. His remarks come after Russia vetoed a U.S.-drafted Security Council resolution on Oct. 30, preventing the renewal of the U.N. Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara, known as MINURSO. A competing Russian proposal also failed, and the mission began winding down Nov. 1. Established in 1991, MINURSO was originally tasked with helping organize a referendum on the territory's future following a ceasefire between Morocco and the Algeria-backed Polisario Front. That referendum never took place, leaving the dispute unresolved. TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS The United States recognized Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara in December 2020 under Trump, a position reaffirmed by his administration in July 2026. In October 2025, the U.N. Security Council adopted Resolution 2797, establishing Morocco's autonomy proposal as the basis for negotiations while maintaining the goal of a mutually acceptable political solution providing for Sahrawi self-determination. Ould Errachid, a Sahrawi politician who grew up in Laâyoune and participated in U.N.-convened negotiations in Geneva in 2018 and 2019, described the proposal as an opportunity for Sahrawis to govern their own affairs. "Except for the king, the Moroccan flag, the currency, the armed forces and foreign affairs, we would have full autonomy to manage our own affairs," he explained. Asked whether the departure of the U.N. mission raised concerns about stability, he rejected the suggestion. TRUMP GETS MAJOR WIN AGAINST CHINA IN AFRICAN RARE EARTH MINERALS RACE "We are not worried. We have a credible project that guarantees a decent future for our people and for our cousins in the Polisario Front," he said. The Polisario Front, which seeks independence, rejects Moroccan sovereignty. Human Rights Watch warned in March 2026 that negotiations centered exclusively on Moroccan autonomy risk undermining Sahrawis' right to self-determination. Beyond the political dispute, Ould Errachid is seeking to translate Washington's support into closer economic ties, inviting American companies to invest in renewable energy, manufacturing, agriculture, water desalination and healthcare. TRUMP SAYS SAUDI NUCLEAR AGREEMENT WON'T MOVE FORWARD WITHOUT ABRAHAM ACCORDS: 'THEY HAVE TO BE A MEMBER' He praised Trump for his 2020 recognition decision and highlighted a major highway connecting Morocco with Western Sahara that has become associated with the president's name. "Nobody here will ever forget the moment President Donald Trump decided to support Morocco. His decision will remain engraved in the history of this region," he said. One example of expanding American engagement is medical cooperation. Laâyoune hosted U.S. medical delegations in February 2025 and October 2026, bringing American specialists together with Moroccan doctors and students. The first gathering produced a partnership agreement between New York's St. Francis Hospital & Heart Center and regional hospitals in Laâyoune. The second resulted in agreements between Laâyoune's Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy and two American organizations, Celenova Fertility and the Fetal Research Fund. According to the organizers, the partnerships are intended to expand medical training, research, student exchanges and specialized care. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Ould Errachid said he is preparing further outreach to American investors in February or March, hoping to expand cooperation beyond medicine into additional economic sectors. "We need your help," he said, describing Western Sahara as a potential gateway for American companies seeking opportunities across African markets.

articles.title: A five-metre dinosaur fossil found at a Surrey quarry in 2001 has been identified as a new species 25 years later; it has been named after a former works manager who died before its discovery
articles.summary: A dinosaur fossil discovered at a Surrey clay works in 2001 has been identified as a new genus and species, more than 25 years after it was excavated.
articles.body: A dinosaur fossil discovered at a Surrey clay works in 2001 has been identified as a new genus and species, more than 25 years after it was excavated. The newly named dinosaur, Paludohadros proudlovii, was a four-legged herbivore that lived around 125 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous Period. The fossil was discovered at Wienerberger’s Ewhurst brick and roof tile works before being donated to the Natural History Museum in London, where it is now preserved.According to the Natural History Museum, the species name honours Will Proudlove, the former manager of the works, who died shortly before the fossil was excavated. The dinosaur was around five metres long and weighed between 1.5 and 2 tonnes, although its bones suggest it was still young.How a 2001 fossil discovery led to the identification of a dinosaurPaludohadros proudlovii was identified from fossils held in the Natural History Museum’s collections. The specimen was discovered at Wienerberger’s Ewhurst brick and roof tile works in Surrey in 2001, then donated to the museum. It belonged to the iguanodontians, a group of dinosaurs known for their distinctive thumb-spikes.For many years, iguanodontians found in southern England were classified as either Iguanodon or its smaller relative Mantellisaurus. A detailed redescription of Mantellisaurus by museum scientists in 2023 helped researchers recognise important anatomical differences between the groups.This has led to several iguanodontians being named in recent years, including Brighstoneus, Comptonatus, Istiorachis and now Paludohadros. Its discovery has added another named dinosaur to the region’s fossil record and its history of discovery.New dinosaur species named after former works manager Will ProudloveThe species name proudlovii honours Will Proudlove, a former Ewhurst Works employee who became its manager. He died aged 35 shortly before the dinosaur was excavated, leaving his wife Rachael and their young children, Ellie and Matt. Rachael said, “Will always had an interest in dinosaur fossils and was fascinated about what, if anything, would be uncovered each time a layer of clay was removed from the quarry. Sadly, this dinosaur was only discovered the year after he died, but its story has become a part of our lives since then.”The family was invited to watch the fossil being excavated in 2001. Rachael said they were overjoyed and honoured that Will’s name and legacy would live on through the dinosaur, which has now been recognised as a new genus as well as a new species.The five-metre herbivore lived around 125 million years agoThe dinosaur lived about 125 million years ago, during the Early Cretaceous Period, when iguanodontians were becoming widespread around the world in the Early Cretaceous. Southern England was then covered in muddy wetlands.The environment also inspired the dinosaur’s name, with ‘palus’ meaning ‘swamp’ in Latin. The animal was a four-legged herbivore, measuring around 5 metres long and weighing between 1.5 and 2 tonnes. That made it similar in size to a rhinoceros. However, its bones do not appear to have been fully developed, suggesting the individual was still a juvenile. The museum said it could potentially have grown twice as large.What do two nearby dinosaur discoveries reveal about ancient lifePaludohadros was found about 100 metres from the site where Baryonyx was discovered in 1983. A two-legged carnivore known for eating fish as well as young iguanodontians. Professor Susannah Maidment, senior author of the research, said, “Paludohadros was found just 100 metres away from Baryonyx, whose fossils we also look after at the Natural History Museum. While Baryonyx is best known for eating fish, this dinosaur’s last meal also included a baby iguanodontian.”“We can’t tell for certain which species this came from, so it’s possible that Baryonyx could have been scavenging on the remains of young Paludohadros or even hunting them when it had the opportunity.”The naming of Paludohadros and other iguanodontians has prompted palaeontologists to re-examine fossils in the museum’s care. Several other Paludohadros specimens have already been identified among fossils collected in the 1950s, and further discoveries may follow as researchers continue.You use AI every day. articles.title: After his family drilled their Ohio farm and leased it to a wildcatter, Barber Riggs saw a well gush 600 barrels in a day; its first check was $50,154
articles.summary: Discover how Barber Riggs' Ohio farm struck oil, generating a remarkable $50,154 initial payment and revolutionizing the family's income with the Barber Riggs No. 2 well in 1980.
articles.body: A productive oil well on the Riggs family’s farm in Washington County, Ohio, began bringing in royalty and override income in 1980, according to a Washington Post report from March 17, 1981. Addie Fields, Barber Riggs’s daughter, told The Washington Post that the well, named Barber Riggs No. 2, produced 600 barrels of oil on its first day, May 26, 1980. Fields said the first oil payment, for $50,154, arrived in August. The details come from Phil McCombs’s March 17, 1981 article in The Washington Post, “Little Oil Wells Yield Ohio Big Money,” which described the oil boom in southeastern Ohio. When the oil was discovered, Barber Riggs was already 94 years old. The daughter of Barber Riggs, Addie Fields, assisted her father in managing the oil business and provided some information to the reporter regarding the well’s productivity and payments. The discovery happened due to the rise in oil prices and as a result of the active drilling of wildcatters in areas in Ohio where oil had not been discovered for low prices before.Barber Riggs No. 2 produced 600 barrels on its first dayFields remembered being informed over the telephone on May 26, 1980 that the well had been gushing oil. She stated that the first day it came in at 600 barrels and then produced 500 barrels per day for two weeks. It maintained production levels of 400 barrels per day for a while before falling off in September. Fields further referred to Barber Riggs No. 2 as the best-producing well drilled in Washington County within the year before. This statement was credited to her and the report was published by the newspaper. For instance, the newspaper noted that a well producing 15 barrels per day was good in the locality. Thus, the initial production was outstanding within the local oil industry. The output, however, did not sustain this initial high level of production.The family received its first payment in AugustEven though the well came in May, the family did not receive their first check until August. According to Fields, the amount paid was $50,154. According to her, it had been frustrating for the family and she believed that the oil company had intentionally delayed making the check to earn interest on the amount. This was a personal opinion and not necessarily an answer to why there had been the delay. Apart from the royalties, the family made some money through another agreement with the operator.Riggs and his relatives had done the original drilling on the land, then leased the drilling rights to a wildcatter. In exchange for giving up those rights, they were paid an override fee. The newspaper analysed check stubs from two wells on the family’s land. From these check stubs, it is revealed that Riggs and relatives got $1430.83 for their one-eighth portion of 350.64 barrels of oil after a windfall profits tax deduction. They also got $423.36 as an override fee and $423.78 from their share of gas sales in the month.Rising oil prices renewed interest in southeastern OhioThe region in southeastern Ohio had been an area where the extraction of oil was prevalent. However, these wells were small-scale and could not yield much. According to The Washington Post’s 1981 report, these small-scale wells had stayed virtually untapped while oil prices were low. Ohio’s wider oil history stretches much further back. The Ohio History Connection says the first oil-producing well in North America was drilled in Noble County, Ohio, where Silas Thorla and Robert McKee discovered oil while drilling for salt brine in 1814. The well, known as the Thorla-McKee well, was located near Caldwell. The Ohio Department of Natural Resources also records that commercial oil and gas production in the state began in 1860. The 1981 report, Little Oil Wells Yield Ohio Big Money, documented how the renewed activity brought additional income to local landowners. articles.title: Carney looks to China as Trump tariffs squeeze Canada's car industry
articles.summary: The PM has suggested Chinese automakers could replace American ones in Canada - but some say that would not be easy.
articles.body:
Canada's car industry has become one of the clearest stress tests for Ottawa as it grapples with US tariffs on the sector.

Now Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that he is looking to China, where he is on a visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit (Apec), as part of the solution.

But that avenue is not without controversy, and is once again drawing the ire of those close to Donald Trump.

While in Cambodia earlier this week, Carney told reporters that Canada could turn to European and Asian carmakers to save its auto manufacturing sector if a trade deal with the US could not be reached.

If Canadian auto workers are "not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities.

"Canada's going to move forward either way," he said.

He went on to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Tuesday for their second head-to-head in less than a year. The two talked of the importance of developing their relations, and Carney said they had agreed to further tariff cuts.

Neither side mentioned vehicles specifically, though analysts suggest the issue will have been prominent in their minds.

In January, Carney said that opening the door to China's electric vehicles (EVs) could result in investment into Canadian-owned companies and the creation of manufacturing jobs in the sector.

American tariffs on imports of Canadian-made vehicles have led to thousands of job losses in Canada and anxiety over the future, as 90% of cars made in Canada are shipped to and sold in the US.

At the same time, China has been eyeing Canada as a potential entry-point to the North American EV market. Earlier this year, Canada announced that it would let in 49,000 EVs from China at a low tariff rate, with plans to raise that quota gradually to 70,000 by 2030.

The move was a significant break from the US, which tariffs Chinese EVs heavily to protect domestic manufacturing.

Peter Navarro, Trump's senior counsel for trade and manufacturing, warned the prime minister against cosying up to China in a post on X .

"Are u really threatening to play China off the US? This is offensive in the extreme," he wrote on Monday. "You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive."

His comments were reposted by Pete Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada.

Chinese EV manufacturers like BYD and Chery have already been lobbying the Canadian government for market access.

Last week, Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu toured a Chery plant in China . He told reporters afterwards that Canadians could expect to see affordable Chinese EVs in Canada by early 2027.

These moves come as the toll of US tariffs on Canada's auto sector has become harder to ignore.

Stellantis, a multinational car manufacturer that made models like the Dodge Challenger in Canada, recently announced it would sell its assembly plant in Brampton, Ontario.

The facility had been idle since 2023 for a planned retooling, but what was supposed to be a temporary shutdown became permanent after Trump's tariffs.

The sale has led to speculation that a Chinese EV manufacturer could move into the facility, after Canadian media outlet CTV News reported , citing anonymous sources, that Stellantis was planning to lease back 25% of its plant to assemble "affordable" EVs.

The idea is unpopular with Ontario Premier Doug Ford. In a letter to Carney, he warned against opening the door for Chinese EV kits to be assembled at the Brampton plant.

China overwhelmingly builds its cars at home and ships them whole - or to be assembled in kits - overseas.

Canada's deal with China signals it is serious about shift from US

How China made electric vehicles mainstream

Lynette Ong, director of the China Governance Lab at the University of Toronto, said introducing Chinese auto manufacturing in Canada would be "controversial" due to fears that Canadian jobs could be lost and that the North American industry could be eroded.

"We want to make sure they're hiring Canadian workers, that they are helping train Canadian workers and that they are transferring the technology over," Ong said.

Carney noted there are "clear guardrails" in how Canada deals with China, including barring work on sensitive matters like artificial intelligence and critical minerals.

Canada has also eyed other partnerships. It is notably pursuing associate member status with the EU, and had signed a free trade deal with the Philippines earlier this week.

Just how much Canada is willing to embrace Chinese manufacturing, however, still depends on the outcome of ongoing US-Canada trade talks.

Progress has been made in negotiations, Carney recently said, but differences remain. It is unclear if Trump and Carney will speak on the sidelines of the Apec summit later this week.

articles.title: We can't afford to hire under-25s, say firms. Will Milburn plans help?
articles.summary: The proposal to cut employers' National Insurance costs is "essential" to tackling the Neet problem, one business group says.
articles.body:
Lowering employers' National Insurance (NI) payments for those between 21 and 24, and cash incentives to take on some workers are among proposals put forward in Alan Milburn's report to get more 18-24 year-olds working.

Many companies have complained that recent increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made it more expensive to take on staff.

We talked to firms and business groups about the issues they face when hiring younger works and what they make of the proposals.

Cutting NI costs is "right in the sweet spot of what firms need to hit the hire button", said the Recruitment and Employment Confederation (REC).

The Milburn report proposes NI thresholds could be raised over the next five years, from £5,000 to £10,000 for those aged 21 to 24, and suggests prioritising the retail and hospitality sectors.

Bournemouth-based café owner Ben Blades says the high costs he faces currently make it difficult to employ young people with no work experience.

"My labour costs are already over 45%. We simply cannot justify the extra cost to put on an extra staff member to train someone up for three months," he says.

"In hospitality our margins have been squeezed and squeezed and squeezed"

As a result, he says it currently makes more sense to employ someone who already has experience.

Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work

At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report

Allen Simpson, chief executive of UKHospitality, says the recommendation to raise the threshold is "the right one" and "would be an immediate shot in the arm for job creation".

But the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) argues the Milburn report does not go far enough in tackling costs facing businesses.

It says while the NI proposal is welcome, the change should be wider than just retail and hospitality, otherwise it "risks adding complexity and blocking off potential career paths".

Other proposals put forward by the Milburn review include cash incentives to employ younger workers.

Employers who take on any young person who has been Neet - not in education, employment or training - for six months should receive a £3,000 payment, and small businesses - with less than 50 employees - that do so should receive an extra £2,000

There would also be an extra £2,000 payment if the young person has been in care or is disabled.

Ally Fir runs a bookshop in Westbourne, alongside her partner Matt, and thinks more state support is needed.

She says incentivised schemes for small business "would help us to employ more, especially young people. If a scheme like that was going we'd jump on it right away."

Fir says she gets job applications "every single day". She'd like to take more people on but "it is the cost of employing people that makes that impossible".

Tom Parsons has already had experience of using government schemes to employ young people at his design consultancy, Aetha, in Poole, Dorset.

The Kickstart Scheme in 2020 meant he could take on two young people in fully funded six-month job placements offering 25 hours a week.

"One of them stayed with us for five years and the other one I think about three years. And it completely changed the game for them," Tom told the BBC. "So if there was a scheme like that, again, that would really help us."

He says he wants to employ young people but costs remain a huge barrier.

Where are the most jobs for 18-24 year-olds?

Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036

One of the government's flagship employment rights reforms risks weakening the hiring of young people, according to Milburn's report.

Ministers are abolishing what they call ''exploitative'' zero-hours contracts and replacing them with guaranteed hours contracts which would be based on the number of hours people normally work.

Much of the detail is yet to be finalised but the Employment Rights Act is due to be enacted next year.

Milburn is concerned that the changes could cause problems "at a time when the youth labour market is already weak'.'

The REC said companies were "particularly worried" over the guaranteed hours measure.

It added that addressing the Neets problem gave ministers "the perfect opportunity" to reconsider the issue.

Young people should have a legal right to a route into education, training or work, and would be supported to do so under an "opportunity guarantee", Milburn has proposed.

This could help firms which are struggling to recruit. Thirty-five-year-old Dean Greene, a sales director at waste management facility Williams Environmental, says it's tricky finding staff.

"We didn't get many applicants for it at all," says Greene, referencing an ad for a marketing and sales role.

"There wasn't a huge uptake from that sort of 16-to-24 range," he adds.

He thinks the lack of applicants may be because the waste industry is perceived as "mucky and dirty", but he is confident many would be interested if they knew the job was available.

Pointing to himself as an example of progressing in the industry, he tells me how he started as an admin officer scanning paperwork at 18 before remaining with the company for 17 years.

articles.title: Priscilla Presley faces a $50 million lawsuit from former business advisers over disputed licensing rights and financial claims; a judge has dismissed four allegations but allowed key fraud claims to proceed
articles.summary: Priscilla Presley is facing a $50 million lawsuit from former business advisers Brigitte Kruse and Kevin Fialko over disputed licensing rights, financial
articles.body: Priscilla Presley is facing a $50 million lawsuit from former business advisers Brigitte Kruse and Kevin Fialko over disputed licensing rights, financial claims, and the terms of their business relationship. A Los Angeles judge has dismissed four allegations but allowed key fraud and breach of contract claims to move forward, according to Rolling Stone and PEOPLE.The case, which began in 2023, centres on claims that Presley abandoned companies formed with Kruse and Fialko to capitalise on her name, image, and likeness. Presley has denied the allegations, calling the lawsuit meritless, while the plaintiffs say they were cut out after Presley’s financial circumstances changed following Lisa Marie Presley’s death.What the judge decidedOn November 16, Los Angeles County Judge Mark Epstein dismissed four of the 21 claims filed against Presley. The dismissed claims involved alleged interference with a cosmetics contract and improper use of Presley’s name, image, and likeness.Presley had also sought to remove paragraphs about her divorce from Elvis Presley and the death of Lisa Marie Presley. The judge described some of the language as gratuitous and mean spirited but declined to strike it, saying the material was already public and removing it would make little difference.The court did allow 10 other claims to proceed, including allegations of fraud, breach of contract, and misappropriation of funds. Judge Epstein gave Kruse and Fialko an opportunity to amend parts of their complaint and potentially revive some dismissed claims under different legal theories.The licensing disputeKruse and Fialko allege that Presley sold certain commercial rights to her name and likeness to Authentic Brands Group in 2005, a transaction they say she concealed from them. Authentic Brands later acquired rights to Elvis Presley’s licensing business in 2013.The plaintiffs claim they worked to secure rights for Sofia Coppola’s 2023 biopic Priscilla, despite Presley allegedly having already sold those rights. The lawsuit argues that this created a conflict over who controlled the commercial use of Presley’s name and image.The judge’s ruling means the fraud claims tied to these allegations can continue. The case will now focus on whether Presley misrepresented her rights or failed to disclose key information to her former partners.Claims about Lisa Marie’s deathThe lawsuit includes allegations that Presley downplayed Lisa Marie Presley’s health issues as part of an effort to control Elvis Presley’s estate. Lisa Marie died in 2023 after being hospitalised with a small bowel obstruction linked to prior bariatric surgery. Presley sought to have these claims removed from the complaint, but the judge declined. He said the material was already public and that striking it would serve little purpose.Presley and her granddaughter Riley Keough have called the allegations untrue and deeply hurtful. In a 2025 statement to PEOPLE, they said their family remains united in love and respect and that their priority is honouring Lisa Marie’s memory and protecting Elvis’s legacy.Presley’s responsePresley’s attorney, Marty Singer, has denied the allegations in the $50 million lawsuit. He described it as one of the most shameful, ridiculous, salacious, and meritless lawsuits he had seen in his practice. Presley filed her own lawsuit in Los Angeles in 2024, accusing Kruse and Fialko of elder abuse. She alleged that Kruse misappropriated more than $1 million and fraudulently induced her to sign agreements giving the pair an 80 percent stake in some of her business ventures.Kruse and Fialko moved their claims from Florida to California and filed a $50 million cross complaint. Their lawyer said the court’s ruling was a victory and that they intend to vigorously enforce their clients’ rights.What happens nextThe case is still in its early stages, and the judge’s ruling does not determine the outcome. It simply means that the fraud and contract claims will move forward, while the dismissed allegations may be refiled under different legal theories.Judge Epstein also expressed frustration with the pace of the litigation. He urged the plaintiffs to act promptly if they intended to add Authentic Brands Group as a defendant, saying the case was getting long in the tooth.For Presley, the ruling means she will continue to face the core of the lawsuit. For Kruse and Fialko, it means their central claims about licensing, fraud, and financial misappropriation will be tested in court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
